author.name: Efficiency Emilia
author.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.

challenge.name: The Loyalty Data Audit
challenge.description: A legal audit flagged that loyalty basket data lacks valid consent records, breaking the legal basis for using it in forecasts. #requirements_reuben# demands the data contracts be fully automated and governed to enforce consent checks before any data enters the pipeline. #efficiency_emilia# argues that manual review is sufficient for now to avoid delaying the promotion planning cycle, though she might accept a middle ground if it does not stall the weekly leaflet.

output.content: I am willing to accept a slower turnaround on the data contract review process if it ensures that consent checks are fully automated and governed. My priority is keeping the weekly leaflet on schedule, so I will trade speed for certainty here. If the pipeline enforces valid consent records before any loyalty basket data enters the forecast, I can live with a manual review step that adds a few days to the cycle. I am not asking for instant approval, but I am asking for a guarantee that we are not processing personal data without a legal basis. Let us automate the checks so I can stop worrying about compliance gaps during promotion planning.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to accept a slower turnaround and manual review steps in exchange for the certainty of automated consent checks, which fits the definition of a trade-off.
